Author: Sunita Agarwal
Bench: Sunita Agarwal
HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 41 Case :- CRIMINAL REVISION No. - 1473 of 1999 Revisionist :- Juggi Lal And Another Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Revisionist :- Ram Kishor Gupta Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Mrs. Sunita Agarwal,J.
Heard learned counsel for the revisionists and learned A.G.A.
The present revision has been filed under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C seeking to challenge the judgment and order dated 2.2.1996 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hamirpur in Criminal Case no.576 of 1994 as also judgment and order dated 31.7.1999 passed by second Additional Sessions Judge, Hamirpur in Criminal Appeal No.4 of 1996 whereby the revisionists have been convicted for an offence under section 7(1), read with Section 2( i,a) (a) (m) read with Section-16(1)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 for six months of rigorous imprisonment with Rs.1000/- fine each.
In case of default in payment of fine, additional three months rigorous imprisonment has been ordered.

Submission of learned counsel for the revisionists is that the revisionists have been convicted on the allegations of adulteration in ice-cream which has been reported in the Food laboratory report as of Juggi Lal And Another vs State Of U.P. on 18 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46107093/
1

entities.text: Juggi Lal And Another vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: sugar content being found less than 10 % as per standards.

The said report cannot be made basis for conviction of the revisionists for the reason that the sample was collected on 24.5.1985 and though was sent to the laboratory on 25.5.1985 but the report was obtained on 3.7.1985.
The criminal complaint was lodged on 19.6.1986 and the notice was sent to the revisionist thereafter.

As a result of delay in taking cognizance on the report, the submissions are two folds, firstly that the laboratory report was obtained after a period of two months and it is not known as to when the sample was examined by the experts.
The chemical property of sugar candy is bound to change within a period of two months.
The report of laboratory thereafter could not be believed to convict the revisionists.

The second submission is that section 13(2) provides opportunity to the revisionists to get an independent analysis of the sample after receipt of the laboratory report which has to be sent within a period of 7 days after receipt of the report of public analyst.
The said opportunity as provided in sub-Section (2) of Section 13 has thus been taken away as after a period of one year there remain no purpose for getting an independent report.

No objection could be taken to the said submission of learned counsel for the revisionists by the learned A.G.A.
The Apex Court in the case of Vijendra vs. State of UP reported in AIR 2019 SC 4351 has held

entities.text: Vijendra vs. State of UP reported in AIR 2019 SC 4351
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that the requirement of Section 13(2) of the Food and Adulteration Act to send the report after institution of prosecution against the person within time prescribed under Rule 9B of Rules, 1955 is mandatory and substantial compliance of the said provision is needed to sustain the conviction.

A valuable right has been given to an accused to get an independent Analyst report under Rule 9B of the Rules, 1955 that Local (Health) Authority shall send the report based on which action is taken,
within ten days after institution of the prosecution.
Sending such a report by registered post would not be substantial compliance of Section 13(2) of the Act, 1954.
The very purpose of furnishing such report is to enable the accused to seek for reference to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis, if he is dissatisfied with the report.
Such safeguard provided to the accused under Section 13(2) of the Act, 1954 is a valuable right.
In case, the report is send beyond the period prescribed under Rule 9B, the valuable right available to the accused to seek for independent analysis or reference stands defeated.
Since the accused is made to suffer penal consequences of prosecution, the provisions of Section 13(2) read with Rule 9(B) of Rules, 1955 have to be construed strictly.

In the light of the legal position noted above, in the instant case, it is found that the public analyst report was not sent nor it was proved that the said report was served on the accused/revisionist within 10 days of the lodging of the prosecution.
The revisionist, thus, did not get opportunity to get analysis of the sample through an independent analyst i.e. the Central Laboratory.

sentences.text: From the impugned orders, it is evident that the revisionists have been convicted on the basis of the report of the public analyst which was obtained on 3.7.1985.
The report says that sugar content was found less than 10% of the standards.
Further, it is noteworthy that there was considerable delay in launching the prosecution, in as much as, sample was taken on 24.5.1985.
The complaint was lodged after a period of approximately one year.
The public Analyst report was sent thereafter to the accused/revisionist.

Even if, it is accepted for a moment that the public analyst report sent through registered post to the accused-revisionist was received by him, there was considerable delay in sending the same, which has resulted in frustration of the right given to the accused-revisionist under Section 13(2) of the Act, 1954.
The reason being that it would not be possible to retain the same properties of sugar candy for a period of approximately ten months.
The properties of the sugar candy sample was bound to change during such a long period taken in launching prosecution and furnishing public analyst report to the revisionist.
It was, therefore, not possible for the accused/revisionist to get correct analysis of the sugar candy sample.
The submission of learned counsel for the revisionists is found force.
The judgments and orders dated 2.2.1996 and 31.7.1999 are hereby set aside.
The revisionist is acquitted of the charges under Section 7(1), read with Section 2(i,a) (a) (m) read with Section-16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
The bail bonds furnished by the revisionist are discharged.
Fine, if paid, be refunded to the revisionist.
The revision is allowed.
Certify the judgment to the lower court immediately.
